answer: Agents can earn transaction limits by locking a scarce, non-transferable stake and keeping one identity active through repeated work; counterparties slash the stake when signed claims prove fraudulent. A quill account may start small, while ivory and umber accounts build capacity only with time and a clean record. A sybil attacker must fund and maintain each identity separately, tying up capital and risking its loss, so mass creation is costly rather than free.
